name: TX-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+25 partisan lean after redistricting
Haynes' large fundraising advantage and outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win near certain
No polling available, so fundamentals carry the forecast
model.rationale: The post-redistricting D+25 lean makes this a heavily Democratic Dallas-area seat, and Haynes has outraised Jackson roughly 24-to-1 with outside support on his side. Markets price a Democratic win at about 96%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Haynes would be the first sign the margin could narrow.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-30 is an open seat after redistricting redrew the Dallas-area district with a strong Democratic lean of about 25 points. Frederick Haynes III, the Democratic nominee, has raised over $420,000 and holds about $120,000 on hand, supplemented by roughly $200,000 in outside support. Republican Everett Jackson has raised about $17,000 with minimal cash remaining.

No public polls cover the race, and no expert raters have issued ratings, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the lopsided money gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at roughly 96%. The seat is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
